elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause limits inspections to once “per year,” which could permit two inspections within a rolling 12-month period.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: HDI must provide no less than 30 days’ prior written notice to the Company.
Inspection is limited to the Company’s normal business hours.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted to HDI’s General Manager, not an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no confidentiality obligation on the person conducting the inspection.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: The clause does not require off-site inspection where possible.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: HDI bears all inspection fees without any underpayment exception, which is more protective of the Company.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause does not prohibit HDI from directly accessing Company systems when inspecting relevant records.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly limits HDI’s inspection right to no more than once per year.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The required 30 days’ prior written notice exceeds the 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: HDI bears all inspection fees without any underpayment exception, which is more protective of the Company.
